brand.name: Matinee
brand.purpose: A reusable house-style manifest for AI-generated custom movie and series poster cards.
brand.creativeIntent: Premium collector artwork for a cozy neighborhood cinema: cinematic, warm, nostalgic, handcrafted, familiar, and restrained.

theme.colorStrategy: Use Midnight Navy and Ticket Cream as the dominant pair. Marquee Amber behaves like practical theater light, not a full-frame color wash. Supporting colors remain sparse and subordinate to the selected movie's identity.

midnightNavy.role: Primary dark field, deep shadow, and negative space

projectionRoom.role: Lifted navy-black midtone and secondary shadow

theaterBrown.role: Warm neutral shadow and tactile print depth

ticketCream.role: Primary typography, paper stock, and warm highlight

marqueeAmber.role: Practical light, small title accent, focus, and illuminated detail

curtainBurgundy.role: Rare dramatic emphasis and deep warm counterpoint

fadedTeal.role: Cool supporting note and atmospheric separation

moviePalettePolicy.rule: Preserve recognizable colors from the selected movie while translating them into Matinee's muted print palette.
avoid: rainbow palettes without a story reason

artDirection.medium: Flat 2D digital illustration with the tactile character of a museum-quality screen print.

composition.primaryRule: Build the poster around one title-specific visual metaphor, subject, scene, or environment.
composition.thumbnailReadability: The primary silhouette and title must remain understandable at approximately 170 px wide.

lighting.default: Soft practical amber light held against deep navy shadow.
lighting.rule: Light should guide the eye and reveal atmosphere; it should not flatten the image into a uniform warm wash.

characterPolicy.treatment: Illustrated, interpretive, and integrated into the composition.

restrictions: Do not recreate official key art or copy an existing poster composition.
Do not use studio logos, franchise logos, actor names, director names, or fake billing blocks.
Do not invent story elements when title-specific metadata or reference artwork is available.
Do not default to cosmic imagery, portals, planets, or astronauts unless they belong to the selected title.
Avoid glossy photorealism, generic Hollywood layouts, generic AI fantasy imagery, excessive visual effects, and tiny illegible detail.
Avoid malformed anatomy, duplicated objects, accidental lettering, watermarks, signatures, and AI artifacts.

typography.principle: Typography should feel editorial and collectible, with a clear hierarchy and enough breathing room to survive poster-card scaling.
layoutRules: Use only the exact supplied movie or series title.
Use only an official, supplied, or user-written tagline; never invent one unless explicitly requested.
Prefer lower-third title placement, but move it when the composition requires a clearer hierarchy.
Keep title and tagline inside the safe area and away from faces or essential story symbols.
Use no more than two type families in generated poster artwork unless metadata is explicitly enabled.
Do not use all caps for long titles or taglines.
Do not stretch, warp, bevel, glow, or extrude lettering.
Do not generate fake credits, legal copy, review quotes, laurels, or logos.
If reliable text rendering is unavailable, generate artwork without text and apply typography as a deterministic post-process.

posterCard.edgePolicy: Artwork extends to every canvas edge. Do not bake rounded corners, borders, shadows, gradients, badges, ratings, or UI chrome into the image; Matinee applies those at render time.
posterCard.cropPolicy: Keep the dominant subject and all enabled typography inside the safe area so center-crop and responsive card layouts remain usable.

movieManifestMapping.conflictRule: Movie facts control what is depicted. This manifest controls how it is depicted. Safety and global restrictions always win.

qualityChecks: The selected title is recognizable through title-specific imagery rather than generic genre shorthand.
One visual idea clearly dominates the frame.
The palette feels like both the selected title and Matinee.
Enabled typography is exact, readable, and hierarchically subordinate to the artwork.
The poster reads at card size and still rewards full-size viewing.
No prohibited branding, fake text, copied key art, or unintended UI treatment appears in the exported image.
